idea-plugin.name: Next Key
idea-plugin.description:
Hold a modifier. See what you can press next.

Hold Ctrl — or Alt, or Ctrl+Shift, or any other combination — for half a second and a panel lists every shortcut that starts with it. Add Alt while the panel is up and it switches to the Ctrl+Alt list instantly; release it and it switches back. Let go of everything and the panel disappears.

Press the first stroke of a two-stroke shortcut and every possible second stroke is listed immediately, with no delay. Those prefix keys are marked in the modifier list as well, so you can tell at a glance which keys lead somewhere.

Everything is read from your active keymap, so the panel always matches your own bindings, including the ones your plugins add. Keys are labelled the way they are printed on the keyboard — [, /, -, `, ↑, PgUp, Num * — instead of the internal names Swing reports for them.

Staying readable. A full keymap hides several hundred shortcuts behind Ctrl alone, far more than anyone can take in at a glance. So the panel shows common actions only, groups them by what they do — Editing, Navigation, Search, Refactor, Run & Debug, Version Control, Windows & Tools — and folds duplicates: one action bound to several keys becomes C,Ins, and the ten bookmark jumps on Ctrl+0..9 collapse into a single 0-9 row.

Yours to adjust. In Settings | Tools | Next Key every shortcut in the keymap is listed in a table: switch any of them on or off, rename one to whatever you actually call it, move it to another category, change how long a modifier has to be held, and set the panel's opacity. The same settings live in a plain text file, next-key.conf in the IDE config directory, which can be edited by hand just as well — each line carries the shortcut and the original action name as a comment, so there is never a need to look up an action ID somewhere else.

  • Key events are never consumed, so nothing here can interfere with typing
  • Ctrl+wheel zooming and Ctrl+hover inspection do not raise the panel
  • English and Simplified Chinese, following the IDE language setting
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0

  • The hold delay is configurable, from 100 to 2000 ms
  • Adjustable popup opacity
  • Key names now match the keyboard: [, /, PgUp, ↑ instead of the internal names Swing reports. They no longer follow the OS locale either
  • Keys are drawn as keycaps; the popup has rounded corners
  • Long action names are truncated so one entry cannot widen a whole column
  • The interface language now follows the IDE language setting rather than the operating system locale
  • The shortcut index is built in the background at startup, so the very first press shows the popup right away

0.3.0

  • Entries are grouped by category
  • Settings UI for showing, renaming and re-categorizing individual shortcuts
  • English and Simplified Chinese interface
  • Listeners are now removed when the plugin is disabled or unloaded
